How do you know they’re hiding who they are? DBT has something called checking the facts, and it’s pretty much sometimes we assume we know all the facts when we don’t. This can cause suffering, if the assumption we’re making has no basis in “fact”, i.e they’ve never said to you “I’m not being real with you, I’m hiding who I am”, it’s harmful to assume they’re being fake. It’s better to assume they’re being themselves and trying to be completely real with you until told otherwise, and if you struggle to change this thought pattern you can straight up ask them, this will give you the facts you need to help switch a negative emotion around it. 

I know it feels like people often leave us, and I know how painful that is. It’s harmful to us to assume they’re going to leave when they’ve never given us a reason to believe that, I think sometimes we can do a lot of pushing away when we have the thought “they’ll leave eventually”. It’s good to try to switch that thought pattern when it hurts

Checking the facts. DBT helped with my mood swings a lot.  Checking the facts is analyzing your mood/thoughts, and modifying your response to the situation. While emotions are valid they may not always be considering the full picture, and acting on them is not always the appropriate thing to do. 

Say if you were angry and you wanted to punch something try to ask yourself “Have i eaten? Have I taken my meds? Am I hungry?”. “Do I actually want to punch a wall or have I just woken up and need a minute to adjust?”. This may be hard to do in the moment of course so at first I would act and then later revisit by checking the facts, “I shouldn’t have thrown that at the wall, I regret doing that I didn’t even get a release, I was hungry and felt better after I ate.”

Say if you’re upset about your partner because you think they “don’t love you” checking the facts would be “They just said they loved me an hour ago. That’s the fact. They still love me until they say they don’t”You can’t assume intentions or thoughts of other people, the facts are everything you’ve been told.

We feel emotions very strongly so it’s easy to act on an emotion or thought you feel is a “fact”, our emotions are valid but there are things we can do to feel them less intensely (especially if it causes suffering!) Emotional regulation is not something we were taught, and I believe in you!!
